facts.text: Sainte-Julie no longer has available land for industrial or commercial development, according to the city.
facts.evidence: Sainte-Julie welcomes numerous businesses, enterprises and industries, but no longer has available land for industrial or commercial development.

facts.text: The city is planning a one-million-square-foot commercial development fronting Highway 20 in its terminus sector, including an office sector.
facts.evidence: the City is currently planning an important commercial development of one million square feet directly fronting Highway A-20 (zone C-247) in the new terminus sector, which will include notably the establishment of an important office sector.

facts.text: Sainte-Julie, along Highway 20, is one of the major industrial sectors of the MRC de Marguerite-D'Youville, with Contrecœur and Varennes.
facts.evidence: The major industrial sectors are located in Contrecœur, Sainte-Julie (Highway 20) and Varennes.

facts.text: Sainte-Julie sits at the crossroads of two major highway corridors close to Montreal and Longueuil.
facts.evidence: Sainte-Julie's strategic positioning at the crossroads of two major highway corridors and its proximity to Montreal and Longueuil make it a privileged setting for business.

meta.descriptor: a South Shore suburb on Highway 20 east of Montreal
meta.fact: planning a one-million-square-foot commercial development fronting Highway 20

overview: Sainte-Julie counted 30,045 residents in the 2021 Census, up only 0.5 percent from 29,881 in 2016. The median age is 44.4, and 11,609 dwellings occupied by usual residents sit on 48.49 square kilometres beside Mont-Saint-Bruno.

The city says it has no land left for new industrial or commercial projects, apart from a large planned development along the autoroute. For a local business, that means a stable, established customer base where growth comes from winning loyal households, not from a wave of newcomers.

byService.lead-generation: Growth of just 0.5 percent since 2016 means Sainte-Julie lead generation should focus on switching and repeat customers among settled homeowners rather than chasing new arrivals.
byService.seo: Sainte-Julie competes with Boucherville and Longueuil for the same searches, so SEO pages should name the city and neighbourhoods like Hauts-Bois in French to win close-to-home queries.
byService.website-development: An older population with a median age of 44.4 values clear text, visible phone numbers and simple booking, so a Sainte-Julie website should favour readability over flashy design.
byService.branding: As the planned autoroute commercial project brings bigger names to town, Sainte-Julie businesses should brand themselves as established neighbourhood choices that residents already know and trust.
